Notes: Popular-front umbrella for the Romanian Communist Party; de facto single list in Great National Assembly elections.

EnglishName: Front of Socialist Unity and Democracy
Notes: Successor popular front dominated by the Romanian Communist Party; only legal electoral list 1980–1989.
Provisional governing front formed during the 1989 Revolution; mixed reformist and neo‑communist currents.
Split from FSN around Ion Iliescu; centre‑left / left‑wing social‑democratic orientation, predecessor to PDSR/PSD.
Anti‑communist democratic alliance of centre‑right and Christian‑democratic parties in the 1990s.
Nationalist party with strong Romanian‑majoritarian and often anti‑Hungarian rhetoric; right‑wing to far‑right over much of its history.

EnglishName: Democratic Union of Hungarians in Romania
Notes: Federation representing the Hungarian minority; generally pro‑EU, regionalist, and moderate on economics but socially conservative on some issues.
Ultranationalist, xenophobic, and often irredentist party; combines welfare statism for ethnic Romanians with authoritarian social conservatism.
Neo‑communist left‑wing party with nostalgia for the socialist era; economically statist and socially traditional.

EnglishName: Party of Social Democracy in Romania
Notes: Mainstream social‑democratic party of the 1990s; direct predecessor of today’s PSD.

SocialCategoryExtended: centre‑left social‑democratic, moderately conservative on some social issues
Notes: Largest Romanian party in the post‑1989 era; combines social‑democratic welfare policies with relatively conservative stances on some cultural issues.
Electoral alliance of PD and PSDR in 1996; pragmatic pro‑EU centre‑left shading towards the centre.

SocialCategoryExtended: centre‑right liberal‑conservative (post‑2000), moderate on social issues
Notes: Successor to part of FSN; moved from social‑democratic towards liberal‑conservative, pro‑market and pro‑EU.
Historic liberal party; economically market‑oriented and pro‑EU, with moderate social conservatism and civil‑liberties rhetoric.
Merger of PD and Liberal Democrats; economically liberal and fiscally conservative, socially more traditional than PNL.
Small conservative party (formerly Romanian Humanist Party); generally pro‑business and socially conservative, often allied with PSD.

SocialCategoryExtended: heterogeneous; mixture of minority‑interest and moderate positions
Notes: Reserved seats for officially recognised ethnic‑minority organisations; ideological positions vary widely.
Non‑party deputies or small local groupings; no coherent shared ideology.
Electoral alliance led by PSD with the Conservative Party; blends redistributive economics with traditional‑values and law‑and‑order themes.

SocialCategoryExtended: big‑tent, centre to centre‑left, moderately conservative
Notes: Grand coalition of PSD, PNL and PC; united mainly by opposition to President Băsescu, mixing social‑democratic and liberal‑conservative elements.
Short‑lived centre‑right alliance (PDL, PNȚCD, Civic Force); economically liberal and fiscally conservative, socially traditional and pro‑EU.
Personalist protest party with redistributive, anti‑elite rhetoric and socially conservative, law‑and‑order messages.
Anti‑corruption, pro‑transparency party; economically centrist/market‑friendly but strongly liberal on civil rights and institutional reform.
Splinter from PNL plus former PC; liberal‑centrist on economics, often aligned with PSD in government, moderately conservative socially.
Party founded around Traian Băsescu; economically liberal and pro‑business, socially conservative and national‑conservative.

SocialCategoryExtended: progressive liberal, socially liberal and pro‑EU
Notes: Electoral alliance of USR and PLUS; centrist on economics, strongly pro‑EU, reformist and socially liberal.

EnglishName: Alliance for the Union of Romanians
Notes: Hard‑right populist party stressing nationalism, social conservatism, anti‑LGBT and Eurosceptic themes; economically mixed but welfare‑friendly for ethnic Romanians.
Recent centre‑right alliance (USR, PMP, Forța Dreptei); fiscally cautious, pro‑market and pro‑EU, but with internal diversity on social issues.
National‑populist and strongly socially conservative party associated with Diana Șoșoacă; highly Eurosceptic and aligned with other hard‑right formations.
